clue.text: Aggressive performance in part of prison-a new cell half destroyed

parts.note: a ward is a section of a prison or hospital

indicators.note: with half of the word cell destroyed, only its front half survives

explanation.surface: A violent display breaks out in a prison wing when a fresh cell is half wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A war dance is a ritual tribal performance done before battle, so it is aggressive by design.

clue.text: Like a certain type of spouse -crafty, full of iron

definitions.text: Like a certain type of spouse

indicators.note: the word for crafty is filled with the iron symbol, which sits inside it

parts.note: crafty and wily both mean cunning
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A cunning partner with a will of iron.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes behaviour typical of a married woman, so it fits a certain type of spouse.

clue.text: Rebuke about home structure on top — if it isn't this?

definitions.text: Rebuke about home structure on top — if it isn't this?

indicators.note: the rebuke goes about, that is around, the word for home

parts.note: to rap someone is to rebuke them sharply
IN means at home
a roof is the structure on top of a house

explanation.surface: Someone scolds the builder about the roof: what if it lets water in?
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue imagines the complaint you would make about a roof that leaks, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof that keeps out wet weather is waterproof against showers, the quality whose absence earns a rebuke.

clue.text: Cultivated area not good it's a forest

indicators.note: not tells us the good abbreviation must be dropped from the cultivated area

parts.note: a garden is an area of cultivated ground

explanation.surface: A garden that is no good, being just a wild forest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forest of ARDEN in Warwickshire is the setting of Shakespeare's As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Arden is the name of a historic English woodland, so it is a proper-name example of a forest.

clue.text: Small child with a look of amusement — or humiliation?

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for child, small signalling the shortening
a grin is a look of amusement

explanation.surface: A small child's grin might be amusement, or embarrassment?
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is mortified annoyance at being made to look foolish, close to humiliation.

clue.text: Jack not wanting fat son provides small fish

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme, Jack Sprat could eat no fat

explanation.surface: Jack, who avoids fatty food, gives his son some little fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme runs 'Jack Sprat could eat no fat, his wife could eat no lean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprats are little herring-like sea fish, eaten whole.

clue.text: Writer given title -one immured and a person no longer working

parts.note: a pen is something that writes

indicators.note: immured means walled up, so the word one is shut inside the title

parts.note: Sir is the title given to a knight
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author, knighted, is walled in and has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone retired and drawing a state or company income is no longer in employment.

clue.text: A foolish person needing a woman

parts.note: a nit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A silly person who needs a woman in their life.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita is a female first name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Somerset's foremost fast bowlers? They can be out of this world!

definitions.text: They can be out of this world!

indicators.note: foremost asks for the leading letter of Somerset

parts.note: in cricket, pacemen are fast bowlers

explanation.surface: Somerset's quickest bowlers are so good they seem out of this world.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is an English county with a cricket team; pace bowlers bowl fast rather than spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts travel beyond Earth, literally out of this world.

clue.text: US plan to be unsuccessful when a Red naughtily intervenes

indicators.note: intervenes means comes between, so the rearranged letters go inside the word for being unsuccessful

parts.note: to fail is to be unsuccessful

indicators.note: naughtily suggests letters misbehaving, so the word Red is rearranged

explanation.surface: An American policy flops when a mischievous communist interferes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughtily' scrambles only 'Red'; the A then follows it, and the pair sits inside the word for failing, after its I. The Fair Deal was President Truman's domestic programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman's 1949 domestic programme was named this, a US government policy scheme.

clue.text: A particular princess is a member of the Iroquois

parts.note: a and one both mean a single thing
Princess Ida is the heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan opera of that name

explanation.surface: A certain princess turns out to belong to the Iroquois.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oneida are one of the original five nations of the Iroquois confederacy in New York State.

clue.text: Stop upsetting neighbour

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the word upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a tuba is a reed stop on an organ

explanation.surface: Stop annoying the people next door.
explanation.definitionFit: To neighbour something is to lie next to it, to adjoin.

clue.text: Bathroom fastener said to be something flowery

indicators.note: said means the words for bathroom fastener are spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a loo pin, a pin for the toilet, as a fastener

explanation.surface: A toilet door bolt described as flowery.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupins are tall garden plants with spikes of blooms, so a lupin is a flowering thing.

clue.text: Butler had to collect wine for religious leaders

indicators.note: to collect means to gather in, so the wine store goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: Rab Butler was a British Conservative politician
had, as in had dinner, means ate
a bin is a rack where wine is stored, standing for the wine itself

explanation.surface: The butler had to go and fetch the wine for the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: Rab Butler was a leading British politician of the 1950s and 60s.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbinate is the body of rabbis collectively, the Jewish religious leaders.

clue.text: Alarm with "Poison!" coming over the loudspeaker

indicators.note: words coming over a loudspeaker are heard, not seen, so we want a soundalike

parts.note: a toxin is a poison

explanation.surface: An emergency warning of poison is broadcast over the speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is a warning bell or signal, so it means an alarm.

clue.text: Moved uncertainly getting cut-the man bloody?

parts.note: a slit is a cut
he is the pronoun for the man
blood is red

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles after being cut, the poor fellow covered in blood.
explanation.definitionFit: To slither is to slide unsteadily, so it describes moving uncertainly.

clue.text: Weight on horse beginning to tell at the outset little energy

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of the word tell

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

indicators.note: at the outset asks for the opening letter of the phrase little energy

explanation.surface: Weight on a horse is told from the start, with not much energy left.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a burden starting to tell on a horse. 'beginning to' takes T from 'tell' and 'at the outset' takes the first letter of 'little energy', where E is also the usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage measures the weight or carrying capacity of a ship or cargo.

clue.text: Afraid bridge player will get involved in a quarrel

indicators.note: getting involved in means joining in the middle, so the player is put inside

parts.note: a ruck is a scuffle or quarrel
in bridge, the four players are North, South, East and West

explanation.surface: A nervous bridge player is drawn into an argument at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Being filled with awe can mean being overwhelmed with fear or dread.

clue.text: Musician in fancy suit coming in under the note

indicators.note: coming in under puts the rearranged word into the following note piece

parts.note: a flat is a musical note lowered a semitone

indicators.note: fancy here means fanciful or elaborate, telling us suit is rearranged

explanation.surface: A player in a smart suit comes in below the note.
explanation.definitionFit: A flautist plays the flute, so is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Red newt found in catalogue

indicators.note: found in puts the newt inside the catalogue

parts.note: a list is a catalogue
an eft is a young newt

explanation.surface: A red newt has been listed in the catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-winger may be called a Red, a socialist or communist.

clue.text: Robin's friend getting food at shop?

definitions.meaning: Friar ... is a companion of Robin Hood
... is British school slang for sweets and snacks, sold at a ... shop

explanation.definitionFit: Friar Tuck is one of Robin Hood's band, and the word is also slang for snacks bought at a school shop.

clue.text: After one drink there's hesitation to get another

indicators.note: after means the hesitation follows the drink

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: After one drink someone hesitates before ordering a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another drink: porter is a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Porter is a dark brown beer, so after port it is a second drink.

clue.text: Like some leaves in tree at end of lane

parts.note: a palm is a tree

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of lane

explanation.surface: A leaf type found on a tree at the end of a country lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaves shaped like an open hand with spreading lobes are described with this botanical term.

clue.text: Little lady wants a pile of rocks? One must pay up!

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young society woman
a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A young woman wants a heap of jewels; someone will have to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocks is slang for diamonds, adding to the false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who owes money is obliged to settle it.

clue.text: I eat lunch on the move that's immoral

indicators.note: on the move suggests letters shifting position, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Eating lunch while walking about is somehow wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' rearranges I EAT LUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without ethics, contrary to right conduct, is immoral.

clue.text: Cross front of promenade to go into fish bar

indicators.note: to go into puts the other pieces inside the fish

parts.note: an eel is a fish
X is a cross shape

indicators.note: front of asks for the first letter of promenade

explanation.surface: Cross the seafront to go into a fish restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to exclude or throw them out.

clue.text: Perhaps a patronising term for a young lady — insult, that is?

definitions.text: Perhaps a patronising term for a young lady

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub or insult them
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Calling a young woman a pet name may be patronising, an insult indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutie is a condescending endearment some use for an attractive girl.

clue.text: The glamour of a cleaner male

parts.note: a char is British slang for a cleaning lady

explanation.surface: The allure of a man who cleans.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm and glamour both mean attractive allure.

clue.text: This person's not everything to communicate

parts.note: this person is the setter, so this person's means I'm
a part is not the whole

explanation.surface: This person is not the whole thing to talk to.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart information is to pass it on, to tell.

clue.text: Schoolboy's toy, a craze -a knock may be received

indicators.note: being received means being taken in, so the other pieces go inside the craze

parts.note: a cult is a fashionable craze
a tap is a light knock

explanation.surface: A fad toy among schoolboys might cause someone a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A catapult is a forked stick with elastic, a classic schoolboy plaything.

clue.text: Spanish city visit -decorated tinware's first thing seen

indicators.note: first thing seen tells us the tinware comes before the visit

parts.note: tole is lacquered or painted tinware
to do a place is to visit it, as tourists do Paris

explanation.surface: On a trip to Spain, painted tin goods are the first sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain.

clue.text: One who works for the rest of the guests?

definitions.text: One who works for the rest of the guests?

parts.words: One who works for the rest of the guests?
parts.note: rest means sleep: a worker in a hotel or college who gets beds ready

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes up the beds at a hotel or Cambridge college serves the guests' sleep.
